chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Musa ibn 'Uthman from 'Ali ibn 'Uthman from Muhammad ibn Hakim who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about something, and he said to me, 'Every unknown matter has the lot (qur'ah) in it.' I said to him, 'Indeed, the lot may err and may be correct.' He said, 'Everything that God has judged by is not erring.'

key_terms.حَكَمَ اللَّهُ بِهِ: That which God has judged by

ai.seo_question: What is the theological basis for using lots (qur'ah) in Islamic jurisprudence according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the principle of *qur'ah* (casting lots) as a valid legal mechanism for resolving matters where evidence is unknown or inconclusive. He counters the potential objection that human error might affect the outcome by asserting that since the mechanism operates under divine decree (*hukm Allah*), it is inherently infallible and free from mistake. This underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that *qur'ah* is not mere chance but a divinely sanctioned tool for justice in ambiguous situations.
